security_problem: SECURITY INVARIANT: an authenticated local controller can monotonically revoke and contain one explicitly enabled supervised stdio session without model mediation. SUPPORTED MODEL: one local Visor process, its launched MCP process group, a protected local control directory, and per-controller HMAC keys. ATTACK CLASSES: unauthorized signal, stale epoch/replay, post-stop call, in-flight side effect, restart/reconnect, control-channel loss, and audit omission/tampering. FAILURE SEMANTICS: enabled initialization and channel integrity fail closed; a valid stop latches before later relay and contains the supervised process group. NON-GOALS: replicas/other hosts, remote execution interruption, fleet control, host-wide process killing, and production-prevention claims.
required_behavior: Default-off local stdio kinetic stop authenticates controller identity and exact command, scopes revocation to session plus monotonic epoch, denies later calls, contains in-flight supervised execution within the documented bound, blocks same-epoch restart, and durably hash-chain audits enforcement.
failure_behavior: Invalid enabled configuration refuses startup; loss or corruption of the enabled control channel contains the current session; unauthenticated commands never gain a controller identity; audit/state failure never resumes a contained session.
non_goals: discovering or stopping replicas on another host (H39 denied edge)
host-wide, SSH, Palisade, fleet, dashboard, or distributed control
default-on, Wiz-fixed, CVE-fixed, or universal production-prevention claims

attack_classes.expected: Unknown controller, malformed command, or bad MAC cannot be attributed as an authorized controller; enabled channel corruption contains fail closed.
Lower epochs cannot revoke a newer session; equal-or-higher authenticated revocation is monotonic and blocks restart through that epoch.
The first tools/call gate and approval recheck deny every call after the revocation latch with zero relay.
The supervised Unix process group and session pipes are killed/closed within the documented operational bound before delayed side effect.
Signed command or authenticated persisted state refuses launch for the same session at a revoked epoch.
An enabled running session contains itself when its protected local control directory becomes unavailable or invalid.
Enforcement emits a synced hash-chained event binding controller, command, target, reason, observed time, epoch, request digest, and resulting state; failure cannot resume execution.
